Issue #47 / PR #48 added optional asynchronous Worker physics and a **Physics mode (reload)** selector to the existing `webgl_loader_mmd.html` example. However, the Examples browser still lists only **Model and animation**, **Audio and camera animation**, and **Poses**. There is no independently discoverable **Worker Physics** example, so visitors cannot launch the feature directly from the gallery or easily compare the default synchronous example to a dedicated Worker preset.

## Expected outcome

Add a **fourth, standalone Worker Physics entry** to the existing Examples browser, reusing the existing MMD model, motion and shared scene infrastructure. The new page should start in `physicsMode: 'worker'` by default without requiring a query parameter or user interaction.

Suggested public page: `examples/webgl_loader_mmd_worker.html` (with a corresponding `.ts` entry point). Keep `webgl_loader_mmd.html` as the existing/default synchronous example, including its current mode selector if practical. The two pages should show the same scene and be comparable, rather than creating a new animation implementation or introducing additional third-party assets.

### Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Create a direct, independently accessible Worker Physics example, e.g. `examples/webgl_loader_mmd_worker.html` + `examples/webgl_loader_mmd_worker.ts`. It requests `physicsMode: 'worker'` at setup by default, and uses the already-supported `workerPhysics.ammoURL` / bundled Worker setup; no query parameter or COOP/COEP headers are required.
- [ ] Add a clearly named **Worker Physics** card/link to `examples/index.html`, with its own `data-example` / hash-navigation identity. Keep all existing cards and Back/Forward, iframe, narrow-screen navigation behaviors. Use an existing correctly attributed preview of the same model if appropriate; no new externally licensed assets are required.
- [ ] Reuse/refactor `examples/scene.ts` minimally so Worker and sync examples share scene setup, camera, model, motion, loading, rendering, controls, and cleanup. Avoid duplicated large HTML/TypeScript scene logic and avoid changing core physics behavior as part of this issue.
- [ ] Show actual runtime physics mode and transport (`worker / shared`, `worker / transferable`, or a clearly explained `sync` fallback), plus the existing measured main-thread helper-update time. Do not label the demo as using Worker unless it actually initialized successfully. Preserve the existing rigid-body and other debug controls where applicable.
- [ ] When Worker initialization fails, surface a comprehensible diagnostic and follow the existing sync-fallback contract; do not silently imply that Worker physics is still running. When SAB is unavailable, Worker should remain usable through transferable buffers.
- [ ] Keep both pages buildable and deployable under the GitHub Pages project prefix, with the correct Worker, Ammo, imports, and generated example asset URLs. Update `scripts/pages-manifest.ts` required page list and relevant deployment/build checks so the new HTML is a verified published artifact.
- [ ] Update `examples/README.md` (and any necessary root README link) with a direct URL, explanation of the dedicated Worker example vs the sync page, transport/fallback behavior, and fair comparison guidance (same scene/device, warmup, main-thread update metric is not an FPS guarantee).
- [ ] Update automated example-browser/tests that currently assume exactly three known example IDs (notably `tests/browser/examples.test.ts`), design/build tests, and Worker integration coverage to assert: the fourth gallery card and hash navigation work; the direct Worker page loads; worker mode is requested and actual mode is visible; and transferable fallback works without isolation. Preserve existing examples, rendering and mobile layout tests.
- [ ] Run and record `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `npm run test:browser`, `npm run build`, and `npm run build:examples`. Include a clear summary of automated and browser validation; do not claim manual performance gains without measurement.

### Required post-merge verification

- [ ] Confirm the GitHub Pages deployment workflow succeeds for the merge commit and the deployment manifest contains the new example.
- [ ] Open the published Examples browser and verify its **Worker Physics** card launches the independently addressable page. Open the direct URL and confirm the real backend/transport readout; verify default sync page still works and a non-isolated deployment can use transferable buffers. Record links, date and results.
- [ ] Keep these publication-dependent checks **pending** until actually executed after merge. Optional hardware benchmarking and subjective hair/clothing latency checks are not mandatory pre-merge acceptance requirements.

## Context

- Physics Worker implementation: #47 (completed via PR #48).
- Existing standard demo: [`examples/webgl_loader_mmd.html`](https://github.com/takahirox/three-mmd-loader/blob/main/examples/webgl_loader_mmd.html); it already supports `?physicsMode=worker` via shared `examples/scene.ts`.
- Examples gallery: [`examples/index.html`](https://github.com/takahirox/three-mmd-loader/blob/main/examples/index.html).
- Build/deployment plumbing: `scripts/build-examples.ts`, `scripts/pages-manifest.ts`, `tsconfig.examples.json`.
- Existing browser tests include an explicit three-item example-ID list, which should become four items.
- Public demo origin: https://takahirox.github.io/three-mmd-loader/examples/

**Scope:** Example discoverability, clear Worker usage and validation only.
